group: Bouncer with a slowly growing zone
title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD1RB_1LF0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD1RB_1LF0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The tape is a short zone followed by the word 111011 repeated. The head sweeps from the zone to the right end and back, adding one unit per sweep, and rewrites the zone at every visit. The zone grows very slowly (77 to 102 cells from step 2,667 to at least 3·108); its map has not been extracted. Direct simulation: no halt in 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,803 cells have been visited and 34,725 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.017). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498).

claims.text: What one visit does to the zone; see the README's For later.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Size of the zone whose map is not decoded.

sections.heading: A zone and a run of 111011
html:
Read left to right, the tape is a zone of fewer than 30 cells for the first 2,500 steps, then between 77 and 102 cells from step 2,667 to at least 3·108, followed by the word 111011 repeated:

step 29,979,814:  1^9 0 1^3 (01)^3 1^2 010 1^11 010 1^7 0 1^3 (01)^4 1^4 0 1^5 0 (111011)^4 (101111)^1287 10 1^3

The head sweeps from the zone to the right end and back. The units are crossed by shift rules (B moving right turns each 111011 into 110101, C moving right turns it into 101110), and every sweep adds 6 cells at the right end: the right side grows like the square root of the step count, the zone hardly at all.

sections.heading: A finite-word map, not extracted
html: The machine halts only in F reading 0 (D reads a 0, writes 1 and moves left onto another 0). The zone's successor at each visit should depend only on the zone and on the phase of the right end, so the question is probably whether the orbit of a map on slowly growing words reaches a halting word. That map has not been extracted. Direct simulation: no halt in 1011 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.017). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,803 cells (24 left of the start, 32,822 right), with a density of 1s of 0.775.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Bouncer with a zone: a short zone (77 to 102 cells from step 2,667 to 3*10^8) and a growing run of 111011; no halt in 10^11 steps; the zone map is not decoded.
